text:
ashwin: heads-up — customer ACCT-1897 (high-traffic payments flow) reported intermittent 401s earlier today. Error from our auth proxy: "jwt: signature verification failed (kid mismatch)". Happening ~1-2% of requests, spike during customer key rotation window. ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACCT-1897 :rotating_light:

maria: can you paste the raw error blob + example request? any commonality in endpoints / regions?

ashwin: yep — sample log:```
ERROR auth-proxy verify.go:142 failed to validate token user=acct-1897 req_id=abcd-1234 err="jwt: signature verification failed" jwt_kid="k_2026_04_a" jwks_cache_kid="k_2026_03_z"
```
Request header snippet:```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImtfMjAyNl8wNF9hIn0... (truncated)
Host: api.redwood.test
X-Region: us-west-2
```
Observed only on the customer's dedicated cluster (us-west-2) and a single model route.

sam: did they rotate their signing keys recently? sounds like our JWKS cache still has old keys and the token is signed with a recently-introduced kid.

ashwin: customer confirmed they rolled a new key at 09:12 UTC. Our JWKS fetch loop has a 5m TTL and an aggressive backoff on 5xx — but they were returning 503s (their key service briefly overloaded) so we didn't fetch the new set for ~7m. During that window tokens with the new kid failed.

elaine: ok — still, we should gracefully handle kid mismatch and try a fresh JWKS fetch instead of failing fast. Ops/infra team — any constraints on reducing cache TTL or adding forced refresh on kid mismatch? @infra-bot can you show current config?

infra-bot: current jwks cache config for auth-proxy:
```
jwks_cache_ttl = 300s
jwks_backoff_on_5xx = exponential (base 5s, max 60s)
jwks_staleness_threshold = 900s
```
Last full JWKS fetch: 1999112000 (returned 200, keys: [k_2026_03_z, k_2025_11_x])

maria: to repro locally I decoded the token header and forced a manual jwks fetch. Steps:```
# decode header
echo 'eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImtfMjAyNl8wNF9hIn0.' | cut -d'.' -f1 | base64 -d
# curl our auth verify endpoint
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://auth-proxy.local/verify?route=/v1/generate"
```
When I hit the proxy with the token and then hit the JWKS endpoint at customer side it returned 503 for ~30s, then 200 with new kid list. Proxy did not refresh until TTL expired.

ashwin: quick mitigation idea: on signature failure where jwt_kid != cached_kids, trigger an immediate async JWKS refresh and retry verification once. That avoids full TTL reduction and handles rotation blips. We should also log a special metric for "kid_mismatch_retry".

sam: agree. Also add owner-oriented observability: emit the token_kid and cached_kids in traces (redact token). customer support can match that to their rotation time.

elaine: one more wrinkle — customer clock skew. Some of the failed tokens also had nbf in the future by ~40s (their signing system clock drifted). Combined with kid issues made repro noisy. We should keep tolerance for clock skew but avoid masking real replays. Current leeway is 60s; maybe increase to 120s for this customer? thoughts?

oncall-sre: increasing leeway is risky globally. I'd prefer targeted leeway per-tenant via config on Dedicated/Kubernetes side. For short-term customer workaround we can allow 120s on their config.

maria: i've drafted a small patch that implements the retry-on-kid-mismatch flow in the verify path. Pseudocode below:```
// verify.go
err := verifySignature(token, cachedJWKS)
if err == ErrSignatureInvalid && token.Kid != cachedJWKS.Kid {
  // fetch fresh jwks async and retry once
  fresh, fetchErr := jwksClient.FetchNow(ctx)
  if fetchErr == nil {
    err = verifySignature(token, fresh)
    metrics.Incr("jwks.kid_mismatch_retry")
  }
}
```
I'll open PR-6723 with tests that stub a flapping JWKS endpoint.

ashwin: thx. What about immediate roll-forward mitigation for this customer? We can trigger an on-demand cache eviction on their auth-proxy instances. @infra-bot — can you evict JWKS cache for tenant acct-1897 in us-west-2?

infra-bot: evict-job queued: job_id=evict-1999112233-1 target=auth-proxy-us-west-2 tenant=acct-1897

infra-bot: evict-job status: success (6/6 proxies evicted), next_fetch=immediate

sam: after eviction, any more 401s?

ashwin: support reports error rate dropped to 0.1% in the 15m after eviction. They still saw a few nbf errors consistent with clock skew. Customer agreed to sync clocks and reissue tokens.

elaine: action items:
- maria -> open PR with kid-mismatch retry and metric (PR-6723) [ETA: 24h]
- infra -> add tenant-scoped jwks_leeway override and eviction API (infra epic) [owner: oncall-sre]
- support -> instruct customer to NTP sync and confirm rotation sequence, add note about short 5xx windows causing missed key pulls (support ticket updated) [owner: sam]
- run a canary config to reduce jwks_cache_ttl from 300s to 120s for non-enterprise customers? (ops discussion)

oncall-sre: I'll schedule the infra task and we can add a synthetic test that simulates JWKS 503 during rotation. Also suggest adding a retry with jitter on the fetch path instead of long backoff on 5xx.

maria: test plan in PR includes a harness that: spins up an auth-proxy instance, a JWKS stub that returns 503 for first N requests then 200, and asserts one retry fetch on kid mismatch. I'll attach logs in PR.

ashwin: thanks team. If anything else pops up from ACCT-1897 i'll post updates here. For historical context, this is different from earlier jwks-stale-cache incidents because that one was TTL misconfig + DNS caching; this is rotation+503 + clock skew combination. Marking as resolved-for-now in support ticket until PR merges and infra changes roll out.

sam: nice writeup. One more small note: can we add explicit log line when we intentionally trigger a JWKS refresh due to kid mismatch? helps correlate with support timestamps.

maria: added that to the patch as "jwks_refresh_trigger=kid_mismatch" in logs.

ashwin: great. closing thread unless someone wants to add follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
